subject: Discovery recap & next steps — inference cost/production fit
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — inference cost/production fit

Alex / Sasha —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the proposed next steps so we have alignment. High-level goal: reduce FinBot's per-inference unit economics while keeping UI latency under the current SLOs.

Pain points you shared:
- Inference cost pressure: model serving spend has grown ~3x YoY and is a top-3 line-item for product budgets.
- Latency for interactive flows: 95th pctl latency ~350–400ms for core flows, which you’d like to get down to ~200–250ms.
- Inconsistent caching/batching: some internal services batch but there’s no centralized KV prefix cache; cold-starts blow up cost.
- Concern about quality regression from aggressive quantization and compatibility with your in-house pre/post-processing.

Current stack (as we understand it):
- Model hosting: self-hosted transformer endpoints on AWS (g4dn instances) via an internal autoscaling layer.
- Orchestration: home-grown request router + light batching at the API gateway.
- Observability: basic request logs, no token-level cost attribution yet.

Success criteria you mentioned:
- Reduce per-request inference cost by >=40% while keeping 95p latency <=250ms for interactive flows.
- No more than a 2–3% drop in model output quality (as measured by your internal evals on the 10k prompt set).
- Ability to run canary traffic for model/quantization rollouts and to fallback to higher-fidelity variants on regressions.

What we recommend (next-step playbook):
1) Technical deep-dive with infra & ML engineering (30–45m) — scope: traffic patterns, exact seq lengths, current batching logic, and KV cache candidates.
2) Performance baseline: we run a short eval on a snapshot of a representative model + prompts to estimate batching gains and latency expectations.
3) Cost modeling: we produce an expected unit-economics delta under several configs (dynamic batching, prefix/KV caching, and 4-bit/8-bit quantization) — aim to show best-case and conservative outcomes.
4) Pilot: 2–4 week pilot on a subset of traffic (non-critical flows) to validate latency and quality with rollback controls.

Open items you said you’d check:
- Confirm the 90–95th pctl latency target (you noted some flows are more latency-sensitive than others).
- Share a sample of the 10k internal evaluation prompts and current seq-length distribution (per our deep-dive).

Proposed dates:
- Tech deep-dive: Tue 4/14 or Wed 4/15 (I’m available 9–12 PT both days)

I’m attaching a short pricing + pilot deck to give a sense of expected outcomes and a SOW template we can adapt if you want to proceed after the pilot.

Attachments: [redwood-pricing-deck.pdf (application/pdf)], [SOW-template.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

Thanks — looking forward to the tech deep-dive.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0199
Redwood Inference — production-grade LLM inference

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finbot.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Sasha Li <sasha@finbot.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 13:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — inference cost/production fit

Thanks Marissa — solid recap and appreciate the clear next steps. A few clarifications from my side: 

- The 95p latency target we care about is for the customer-facing chat + recommendation flows; aim is <=250ms. Internal batch jobs (analytics) are not sensitive.
- Seq-length distribution: median ~128 tokens, 95p ~620 tokens (we’ll export and share the histogram prior to the deep-dive).
- Concurrency: typical concurrency per endpoint is 8–16 during peak; spikes can go higher but those are less common.
- Quantization: we are open to 4-bit/QLoRA-style approaches if we can run an A/B and see no more than ~2% drop on your suggested evals.

For the deep-dive, please include someone who can speak to KV/prefix caching capability and rollout mechanics (fallback to full-precision model). Ben — can you join the 4/14 slot if it works for Marissa?

I’ll have Sasha share the prompt set and the seq-length export by EOD Monday. Also looping in procurement later this week for standard SOW review.

—
Alex Chen
Head of Infrastructure, FinBot
alex.chen@finbot.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — inference cost/production fit

Thanks Alex — perfect. Quick notes before the deep-dive:

- We’ll scope the deep-dive to focus on the chat + recommendation flows (95p latency target <=250ms).
- Our perf engineer (Ben) will cover batching strategies and how we’d integrate prefix/KV caching with FinBot’s router — plan is for the caching layer to sit between your API gateway and model runtime so no changes to the frontend.
- For quantization: typical playbook is run a parallel A/B with a canary that uses 4-bit quantized model variants and an automatic rollback if downstream evals/QA flags exceed thresholds. We’ll include signal hooks for your eval harness.
- Cost modeling: we’ll provide a conservative and an optimistic scenario (optimistic assumes good hit-rate on KV cache + steady batching gains).

Ben — assigning you action item to prepare a short (5–7 slide) appendix on batching: current batching heuristics we’d suggest, expected throughput changes, and impact on p95 latency for seq-length bins (median, 95p). Can you have that ready for the deep-dive?

Proposed meeting: Tue Apr 14, 10:00–10:45 PT. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite with a short agenda + pre-reads.

Thanks — attaching the one-page pilot + pricing snapshot again for reference.

Attachments: [redwood-pricing-deck.pdf]

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
